sections.h2: Where is Gallatin County, Montana, and what does it include?
sections.html:
Gallatin County is in southwest Montana, its seat is Bozeman, and it was created in 1865. It takes its name from the Gallatin River, which Meriwether Lewis named in 1805 for Treasury Secretary Albert Gallatin. The Wikipedia entry gives 2,632 square miles of total area and a 2020 census population of 118,960, the second highest in the state.

The cities are Bozeman, Belgrade and Three Forks, and the towns are Manhattan and West Yellowstone. Census-designated places include Big Sky, Gallatin Gateway, Four Corners, Bridger, Logan and Springhill. The Bridger Range rises in the north and the Gallatin Range in the south. Interstate 90 crosses the county, along with U.S. Highways 20, 191 and 287.

At the south end, the West Yellowstone entrance to Yellowstone National Park accounts for about half of all park visitors, and Big Sky Resort lies partly in Gallatin and partly in Madison County. Part of the Gallatin National Forest and Yellowstone National Park fall inside the county line.

sections.h2: What shapes the Gallatin County economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Montana State University and Bozeman Health anchor the local job base. The university's flagship campus is in Bozeman, and Bozeman Health says it is the largest private employer in Gallatin County, with a hospital campus about five miles from the university and a medical center in Big Sky.

Growth is the other big factor. The Gallatin County Triangle Community Plan notes that since 2010 the county has been one of the fastest-growing in Montana. The City of Bozeman's 2025 to 2045 forecast puts Bozeman at 87,400 residents, which it describes as nearly half the county's projected total, and a 2025 Gallatin Valley housing report credits the economy and the turnover of a young population around the university.

This shows up in property tax. The Census median owner-occupied value for the county, $604,900 as shown earlier on this page, is well above the $378,000 first-bracket line used in the 2026 rate schedule, so many primary residences here pay at more than one rate.

sections.h2: How are Gallatin County homes taxed for 2026?
sections.html:
A principal residence pays 0.76 percent of the first $378,000 of market value, 0.90 percent of the portion from $378,001 to $756,000, 1.10 percent up to $1,511,999 and 1.90 percent above that. The Department of Revenue explains the tiers on its 2026 information page. A second home, short-term rental or vacant residential lot pays a flat 1.90 percent.

Working through the county median as an illustration: 0.76 percent of $378,000 is $2,872.80, and 0.90 percent of the remaining $226,900 is $2,042.10, for roughly $4,915 of taxable value. At the flat 1.90 percent rate, the same house would carry about $11,493. Local mills, which vary by city, school district and special districts, are applied to that taxable value afterward.

ItemMontana rule
Homestead eligibilityOwner lives there at least 7 months of the year

Rate after a saleStays through the calendar year; new owner must apply by March 1
Eligible homesSingle-family, townhome, condo, manufactured home with up to 1 acre

Because resort areas such as Big Sky sit inside the county, a seller should confirm which rate class the property was in. A buyer who plans to move in will usually want the homestead rate for the next year.

sections.h2: When are Gallatin County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Montana splits the bill in two: half is payable by 5 p.m. on November 30 (or within 30 days after the notice is postmarked, if later) and half by 5 p.m. on May 31. Montana Code 15-16-102 sets the dates.

Homeowners who enroll in the alternative payment schedule for a primary residence instead make seven near-equal payments, due on the last day of each month from November 30 to May 31. Missing any scheduled payment makes the amount delinquent, with the same 2 percent penalty and monthly interest. A taxpayer may pay the current year without first paying older delinquent taxes, but money sent toward delinquency is applied to the oldest year first.

When selling, ask the title company which half has been paid, since the unpaid half and any partial-year share can affect the closing statement.

sections.h2: Who do you contact about Gallatin County property tax?
sections.html:
Payment questions go to the Gallatin County Treasurer, and valuation questions go to the Montana Department of Revenue. The treasurer's office is at 311 West Main, Room 103 in Bozeman, with phone numbers listed at 406-582-3033 and 406-582-3030. The county's tax pages point valuation questions to the Department of Revenue Bozeman Office at 406-582-3400, or dorgallatinoffice@mt.gov.

  • Treasurer: tax bills, payments, delinquent taxes, tax liens and assignments.
  • Department of Revenue Bozeman Office: appraisal, classification, corrections to property characteristics.
  • Clerk and Recorder: receives direct appeals to the county tax appeal board.

The county also advises owners to keep the Department of Revenue's mailing address current, because the notices of pending liens go to the last known address on file. You can update an address by emailing the Bozeman office.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent taxes and tax liens in Gallatin County?
sections.html:
A payment after the due date is delinquent immediately, with a 2 percent penalty and interest of 5/6 of 1 percent per month, and a lien must be attached if real property taxes stay unpaid by the first working day in August. The county's tax lien timeline explains the sequence under Montana Code 15-17-125.

The county sends a courtesy notice after the first half becomes delinquent. After the second half is delinquent it publishes a notice in the Bozeman Daily Chronicle, and two weeks before the first working day in August it mails pending lien notices. If the tax is still unpaid on August 31, another person can take an assignment of the lien by paying all taxes, penalty, interest and costs, including a $60 fee in the timeline's 2023 example.

One detail is specific to Bozeman. The city forwards delinquent special assessments to the county for collection, so an owner can have paid county property tax and still face a lien for unpaid Bozeman special assessments.

  • August 1 (first working day): liens attach to still-delinquent properties.
  • August 15: earliest date an assignee may mail the required notice of pending assignment.
  • August 31: first day assignments can be purchased.
  • September 1: most assignments are issued.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Gallatin County valuation and pay under protest?
sections.html:
File Form AB-26 with the Department of Revenue within 30 days of the date on your classification and appraisal notice, or take the matter straight to the county tax appeal board through the clerk and recorder in the same 30 days. The department's appeals page also describes the Montana Tax Appeal Board, whose decisions are final unless you go to district court.

To keep your right to a refund with interest, Montana law requires a written protest filed with the county treasurer and payment of the disputed tax by the due date. Taxes must be paid before they become delinquent for the protest to count. For the current cycle, supporting evidence is measured against a January 1, 2024 valuation date.

faqs.q: Who sets my Gallatin County property value?
faqs.a: The Montana Department of Revenue. The county treasurer bills the tax, and the department's Bozeman Office at 406-582-3400 answers value and classification questions.

faqs.q: What happens on August 1 if my taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: The county treasurer attaches a tax lien to real property with delinquent taxes as of the first working day in August, and files it with the Clerk and Recorder. A copy goes to the owner's recorded address.

faqs.q: Can I owe Bozeman special assessments even if I paid county tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Bozeman forwards delinquent special assessments to the county, and they become part of the county's collection process, so a lien can attach for them.

faqs.q: How much is the 2026 rate on a Gallatin County second home?
faqs.a: A flat 1.90 percent of market value applies to second homes, short-term rentals and vacant residential lots, compared with tiered rates starting at 0.76 percent for a primary residence.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Gallatin County house for cash with a lien on it?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the lien, penalty and interest from the sale proceeds at closing, and a cash buyer does not need lender approval to proceed.
